content.text: Writing Step 4, the day-to-day workflow:

from.content:
## Step 4: Daily workflow

1. **Start a trail for each feature** (a trail is Entire's version of a pull request). From your branch:
    - `entire trail create --title "What you're building"`
2. **Work with Claude Code as usual:** run `claude` in the repo folder and give it tasks.
3. **Commit and push your branch.** The checkpoint is attached on its own (you'll see an `Entire-Checkpoint:` line in the commit message). If git asks whether to link the commit to session context, answer `Y`.
    - `git add <files>`
    - `git commit -m "..."`
    - `git push origin <your-branch>`
4. **See the team's work:** `entire trail list --project gh/nougify`, or open [the project on entire.com](https://entire.com/gh/nougify). Review agents (once Jerry turns them on) run on every push and post findings to the trail.
5. **Optional local review before pushing:** type `/code-review` inside Claude Code. It runs on your own Claude plan.

content.text: Last section, troubleshooting:

from.content:
## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `entire: command not found` | Close and reopen your terminal. Still missing → reinstall from Step 2. |
| `no read access to repo (403)` on clone or push | You haven't accepted Jerry's GitHub invite, or Jerry hasn't granted Entire access yet. Ask Jerry. |
| `entire trail show` gives 403 with no arguments | Known issue. Use `entire trail show <number> --project gh/nougify` instead. |
| `entire api /api/v1/...` says the path must be origin-relative (Git Bash on Windows) | Prefix it: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 entire api /api/v1/me`, or use PowerShell. |
| Commits have no `Entire-Checkpoint:` line | Run `entire enable --agent claude-code` again inside the repo, then `entire doctor`. |
| Keychain or network error inside a sandbox | Run the command in a normal terminal. Don't log in again. |

Still stuck? Run `entire doctor` and send the output to Jerry.

content.text:
You work in parallel the way you would with Git: everyone gets their own branch and their own trail, and you merge into `main` when a feature is done. Entire adds the shared view of everyone's sessions and reviews. Each person runs Claude Code on their own account at the same time, so nothing blocks anyone else.

**The workflow:**

1. **Split the work by area.** For example, one person on frontend, one on backend, one on data or infra. Tasks that touch different files rarely conflict.
2. **Each person, per feature:**
   ```
   git switch main && git pull
   git switch -c <name>/<feature>
   entire trail create --title "<feature>"
   ```
   That gives each feature its own trail, and Entire's version of a PR.
3. **Work and push often.** Each commit includes that person's Claude session, and review agents run on every push.
4. **See what everyone's doing:**
   ```
   entire trail list --project gh/nougify
   entire trail timeline <number> --project gh/nougify
   ```
   You can also open https://entire.com/gh/nougify to see every trail, commit, session and finding in one place. If someone gets stuck, `entire trail resume <repo>/<n>` picks up their Claude session where they left off.
5. **When a feature is done:**
   ```
   entire trail ready <number>                # ask for review
   entire trail approve hackcamp27/<n>        # a teammate approves
   entire trail merge hackcamp27/<n>          # merges into main
   ```
6. **Stay in sync.** After someone merges, everyone else runs `entire trail update-branch` (or `git pull origin main` on their branch) so conflicts are small and caught early.

**Rules for a hackathon:**
- Never commit directly to `main`. Merge through trails only.
- Keep features small and merge every few hours, not once at the end.
- If two people need the same file, agree on who owns it, or merge one of them first.

content.text:
Reviews can now run on your own Claude accounts instead of Entire's billing. I set up a shared review profile that uses each person's local Claude Code and posts the verdict to their trail. It's committed and pushed to your `jerry` branch.

**How each person uses it:** from their feature branch, before or after pushing, run:
```
entire review
```
Claude Code reviews the branch against `main`, a final "judge" pass combines the findings, and the verdict appears on that trail at entire.com. It uses whoever ran it's Claude plan, and needs no Entire billing.

**Things to know:**
- **Teammates only get the profile after `jerry` is merged into `main`, or after they pull `jerry`.** Until then they can create it themselves with `entire review --configure --set-agents claude-code --set-judge claude-code --set-output trail`.
- **It doesn't run on its own.** Someone has to type `entire review`. Entire's automatic on-push reviews are server-side, so they need billing or the free presets.
- **Reviewing a teammate's work:** `entire review --target <trail-or-branch>` reviews it using your Claude account.
- **Two reviewers:** `entire review --configure --set-slot claude-code --set-slot claude-code` runs two Claude reviewers in parallel. It's more thorough but uses more of your plan.
- `entire review` is a labs (experimental) feature, so expect some rough edges.

If you also want automatic reviews that cost nothing, the free presets still work: `! entire project agent add code-review security-review`.

# Team workflow (Entire + Claude Code)

This repo uses Entire. Commits capture the Claude session as a checkpoint automatically. Run `entire agent-help` for exact CLI flags.

## Branches and trails
- Never commit to `main`. Work on a feature branch: `git switch main && git pull && git switch -c <name>/<feature>`.
- Each feature gets one trail: `entire trail create --title "<feature>"` (skip if the branch already has one: `entire trail list --project gh/nougify`).
- Keep features small; merge every few hours.

## Before pushing
1. Run `entire review` (profile `general`: local Claude Code reviewers, verdict posted to the trail). This uses the user's Claude plan, not Entire billing.
2. Fix or report every finding it raises before pushing.
3. Commit, then `git push origin <branch>`.

## Finishing a feature
- `entire trail ready <number>` to request review. A teammate approves (`entire trail approve hackcamp27/<n>`) and merges (`entire trail merge hackcamp27/<n>`).
- After someone else merges, sync: `entire trail update-branch` or `git pull origin main`.

## Gotchas
- `entire trail show` with no args returns 403; pass the number: `entire trail show <n> --project gh/nougify`.
- In Git Bash, prefix `entire api` calls with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`.
- Ask the user before `entire enable/disable/clean/login` or granting project access.
